story_text.value:
Hey HN! I built https://callmylaptop.com, an app that lets you access the coding agents running on your laptop by phone.

Call My Laptop has three key features: 1) it gives your laptop its own phone number, 2) it lets you start a new or resume an existing Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode session by phone, and 3) it calls you when a task finishes or needs your input.

I hope Call My Laptop makes coding agents easier and more fun to use away from your desk. I've personally been using it a bunch when I'm riding my bike to spin up sessions on random ideas :).

Happy to chat about the voice, telephony, or dev stack behind the product. Let me know if you have questions, comments, or feature requests!

story_text.value:
I make this tool, a self-hosted dashboard, to show which host ports are taken, as a traffic-light grid. All the reason because I'm a home server enthusiast, but have a chaotic and terrible memory.
It can aggregate ports from your different hosts and VPS as long as the network is reachable. And it merges three local sources into one grid: host listen tables, Docker API, and Compose files.
As a beginner, I am open to everyone's comments, and if there are better similar tools, please tell me about them to help me refer to them for learning, thanks.

story_text.value:
I've seen a few of those "Every fucking website in 202*" examples on here the last few days, and I feel it deep in my bones.

As a result of the constant auto-play videos, CTAs, cookie warnings etc. etc., this is probably the most used self-developed app I run. It's super simple - just drop in the URL of the article and it'll extract (maintaining structure, formatting, pullquotes, images etc.) and save into an SQLite library if you want to come back to it later.

Saves nicely as a PWA for tablet / phone reading.

story_text.value:
It bothered me that despite all the space on my laptop screen or desktop monitor, reading web articles felt like breathing through a straw. Horizontal space is poorly used and vertical space is in short supply, leaving only a few paragraphs on screen at once.

Columnary is a Chrome extension that makes full use of your screen real estate, whether it's a small screen laptop or a 5K monitor. It strips ads and formatting, and puts everything into columns in a horizontally scrolling format. This way, articles can fill 100% of your screen while keeping line lengths readable.

This transforms the way your brain processes articles. When you can see the whole thing at once, you can utilise your natural spatial processing ability to make sense of where you are.

Columnary also includes a bookmark feature so you can mark your place when stepping away from long articles, and various typography settings and a full screen mode, as well as keyboard shortcuts to help you scroll by column.

Source code is at https://github.com/kevinwuwon/columnary

title.value: Show HN: Columnary, a better experience for reading long articles
